items.title: Peel school board ‘deeply saddened’ after Mississauga and Brampton teens killed in crash
items.summary: , just outside Guelph. The school board that operates schools in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon says one current and two former students were among those who died in the single-vehicle crash over the weekend. Ontario Provincial Police said at a news conference Sunday they’re investigating if a lack of seatbelts contributed to the fatal crash, which also injured two others. The OPP said six young people from the Greater Toronto Area were travelling along Watson Road South early Saturday when the car left the road, struck a guardrail and careened into a ravine. Police said a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 15-year-old girl from Milton and two 19-year-old men hailing from Mississauga and Brampton died in the crash. Police said Sunday that a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga remained in hospital with life-altering injuries after the crash, while a 16-year-old from Mississauga sustained non-life-threatening injuries. The school board extended its condolences to the families and friends of the deceased and says it is providing support to students, families and staff impacted by the incident. Given the ongoing investigation, the board says it will not comment on the matter further.

items.title: Violent incident at UTM in Mississauga ends when gunman reportedly takes own life
items.summary: Peel police officers fired multiple rounds from anti-riot weapons but did not use their guns in trying to apprehend an armed man who subsequently died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound early Tuesday morning at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, Ontario’s Special Investigations Unit said. The SIU, which took over investigation of the incident Tuesday morning, said Peel Regional Police officers discharged ARWEN devices as they attempted to arrest the 19-year-old suspect on Monday night inside a student residence at the Mississauga Road university campus. ARWEN devices, or anti-riot weapons, fire less-lethal rounds designed to incapacitate a suspect so as to prevent them from harming themselves, bystanders or police. m. in the bedroom of a student residence at the Dundas Street West/Mississauga Road area campus. m. Officers on the scene quickly realized the armed man they were dealing with was wanted in connection with a Monday afternoon domestic assault in Brampton in which a suspect was reportedly in possession of a gun. Peel police Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, who also briefed the media at the university campus on Tuesday morning, said officers spent several hours negotiating with the suspect while he was barricaded inside one of the townhouse-style student units. Bell-Morena said a number of frightened students reported hearing what they believed were multiple gunshots, but what they actually heard was police ARWEN weapons being discharged in attempts to subdue the suspect.

items.summary: Peel Public Health officials issued conditional passes to Food World Plus, Fuwa Fuwa Japanese Pancakes, Pure Punjabi Sweets & Restaurant and Lazeez Shawarma. The Peel Public Health inspection program is designed to provide the public with information about inspections of food establishments. Peel Public Health officials issued conditional passes to several Mississauga food-serving businesses, including a newly opened supermarket, during recent inspections. Inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries, takeout food establishments and other types of businesses to ensure compliance with safety standards. items.title: SIU investigates after man found dead at University of Toronto Mississauga campus, shelter-in-place lifted
items.summary: The university issued the shelter-in-place alert after reports of an armed individual at the campus late Monday night. Police investigate at the McLuhan Court Residence at Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road on the University of Toronto Mississauga campus. The province’s police watchdog has invoked its mandate after a 19-year-old man was found dead following reports of gunshots and an armed individual at the University of Toronto’s Mississauga campus on Monday night, authorities said. The university says the overnight incident has “been resolved” and there is no threat to public safety. The University of Toronto issued a shelter-in-place order Monday night for its Mississauga campus after reports of gunshots. , Peel police responded to reports of an armed individual inside the McLuhan Court Residence at Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road. After officers arrived on scene, the suspect fired a gun from within a unit, police said in a statement Tuesday morning. Officers then moved to evacuate the building and the surrounding area.

items.title: Dredging of marsh to be completed by end of 2026 in Mississauga
items.summary: The year-long dredging of a northwest Mississauga marsh in an effort to protect that part of the city from flooding is expected to be completed next month. City of Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. ” The first-ever dredging of the man-made stormwater pond began in September/October 2025 and is being completed so it can better perform its important function, city officials said earlier. The major project is part of the City of Mississauga’s stormwater management program, with specific emphasis on flood prevention in the Lisgar district, McFadden said. “The marsh will be dredged by barge and the pond is not expected to be fully drained except for the very northeast cell where sediment will be deposited, dried and then trucked away,” McFadden explained in an update to constituents earlier this year. ” (Image: Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden newsletter/City of Mississauga) Osprey Marsh, located to the immediate northeast of Britannia Road West and Ninth Line, was built in the mid-1990s and is undergoing its first dredging. Preparation work began in September 2025 and the dredging started in October 2025. Various sections of trails were also closed at that time to allow the work to proceed.

items.title: Mississauga moves to expropriate two Port Credit homes after 18 months of ‘lawlessness,’ city councillor says
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is attempting to expropriate two houses in the municipality’s Port Credit neighbourhood after the property saw hundreds of visits from police, firefighters, and bylaw officers over the past year-and-a-half. It is a move that one expert says is a somewhat novel application of expropriation laws more commonly used to clear the way for the development of major infrastructure projects, like subways. But Mississauga city councillor Stephen Dasko told CP24 last month that the city has exhausted all other options to deal with the slew of complaints at the properties over the past 18 months. The homes, located at 34 and 36 Peter Street, are across the street from Riverside Public School and a few doors down from the Mississauga Long Term Care Facility, located in the area of Mississauga and Lakeshore roads. com on Oct. 7. ” “These incidents resulted in more than 50 arrests, with numerous charges laid,” police said in an email to CP24.

items.title: Modern Travel: Adventure Aplenty in North Bay, Ontario
items.summary: After spending a few days in North Bay, the gateway of the north, I half-jokingly thought of calling it “North Jay” given the excellent experience I had. There’s certainly a charming, small-town feel here, heightened by being warmly welcomed throughout my visit. The was kindness and friendliness wherever I went and their approachability compass points straight north. Here’s my North Jay, err, North Bay adventure and I invite you to either follow my footsteps and paddle strokes, use this as a guide for your own explorations or balance a bit of both. I hope this inspires you to spend time in North Bay and if it does, tag Modern Traveller in your social posts.

items.title: New Lego Store Set to Open at Square One This Friday, Completing GTA Trifecta
items.summary: The Lego Group says its new store at Mississauga's Square One Shopping Centre opens Friday, Nov. 6. According to the company, the roughly 2,970-square-foot store sits on the second floor in Unit 2-212, between La Vie en Rose and Indochino. The Lego Group said the Square One location completes a trio of new Lego stores opened across the Greater Toronto Area this fall. A Lego store opened at Markham's CF Markville in September, followed by another at Toronto's CF Eaton Centre in October. The company confirmed the Square One store would open to shoppers Friday morning, marking the third Lego-branded retail location to open in the GTA within about two months.
